facts.title: Mixture-of-Kittens：面向 NVL72 的开源 MoE 兆内核
facts.event_hint: Cursor 开源 Mixture-of-Kittens（MoK）确定性 MoE 训练兆内核，融合 NVL72 上的通信与计算
facts.problem: Cursor reports that the MoE layer was a major bottleneck in Composer training because communication could take as long as computation, while CPU-side work and synchronization could leave GPUs idle on GB300 NVL72 systems.
facts.mechanism: MoK fuses MoE dispatch/combine communication, expert FFNs, and scheduling into one deterministic megakernel. It uses pull-based forward dispatch and push-based combine, device-side schedules, inter-SM communication/computation overlap, tunable minibatches, a fixed-size ring token buffer to avoid CPU-GPU synchronization, CLC for RDMA overlap, and fused MXFP8 quantization.

evidence.claim: On GB300 NVL72s, MoK achieved up to 2.37x higher MXFP8 forward throughput than the fastest public baseline.
evidence.condition: MXFP8 forward; GB300 NVL72; MoE layer benchmark
evidence.source_locator: Heading: Mixture-of-Kittens achieves up to 2.37x higher MXFP8 forward throughput

evidence.claim: Under expert imbalance, pull-based communication delivered up to 29% higher NVLink bandwidth utilization than push-based communication.
Push-based dispatch signalling incurred roughly 5.8x higher latency than pull-based dispatch signalling, 103 microseconds versus 18 microseconds.
MoK's end-to-end production training throughput was 1.41x the DeepEP-based setup, with 1,070.2 versus 760.9 tokens per second per GPU.
evidence.condition: 512 GPUs across several GB300 NVL72 racks
evidence.source_locator: Section End-to-end benchmarks; table DeepEP-based MoK Tokens / second / GPU

evidence.claim: The MoE layer benchmarks ran within one NVL72 rack with expert-parallel degree 64 and 2,048 tokens per GPU before routing.
evidence.condition: single-NVL72-rack forward/backward BF16 and MXFP8 benchmarks

facts.evaluation_context: The post describes MoE-layer benchmarks on GB300 NVL72s using BF16 and MXFP8, EP degree 64, 2,048 tokens/GPU, four model shapes, and baselines including NCCL+PyTorch, DeepEP variants, and HybridEP+Megatron. End-to-end results use 512 GPUs across several GB300 NVL72 racks and compare against a DeepEP-based production stack.
facts.limitations: The source is a Cursor engineering post and is marked discovery_only, so primary-source resolution remains false; benchmark methodology and graphs are not independently reproduced here. Results are on GB300 NVL72-specific shapes and may not transfer to other GPU fabrics, workloads, or model configurations. The reported end-to-end result comes from Cursor's internal training stack.
facts.project_relevance: MoK provides a concrete example of coupling GPU communication direction, scheduling, and computation to reduce MoE training overhead. For this project, its device-side scheduling, deterministic execution, and explicit overlap controls are useful design references, but NVL72-specific gains should not be generalized without comparable measurements.
source_notes: The full Cursor engineering post was fetched and supports the listed claims; the linked GitHub repository was not opened in this task.
Because the candidate is marked discovery_only, primary_source_resolved is intentionally false.
